expectation: The board oversees IT and approves an IT strategic plan aligned with business objectives.
Management maintains an IT risk management process to identify, measure, mitigate and monitor IT risk within board-approved risk appetite.
IT policies, standards and procedures are documented, and IT roles and responsibilities are clearly assigned.
Management provides adequate staffing, skills and budget for IT operations and projects.
Management reports IT performance, risk and significant issues to the board on a regular basis.
The institution complies with applicable laws and regulations including the GLBA Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards.
The board approves the information security program and management promotes a security culture with clear accountability.
The institution identifies threats and vulnerabilities to its information and systems.
Hardware, software, data and connections are inventoried and classified by criticality and sensitivity.
Identified risks are assessed for likelihood and impact and prioritized for mitigation.
Information security policies and standards are documented, approved and kept current.
Access is granted on least privilege and need to know with authentication commensurate with risk and periodic access reviews.
Networks are segmented and protected with boundary controls and secure remote access.
Endpoints and servers are hardened and protected against malicious code.
Changes to systems are authorized, tested, documented and approved before implementation.
Sensitive information is protected in storage and transmission and when disposed of.
Security is built into application development and acquisition.
Security requirements are defined for service providers and their controls are monitored.
The institution obtains and evaluates threat intelligence relevant to its environment.
Systems and networks are monitored and logs are reviewed to detect anomalous activity.
The institution maintains an incident response program covering detection, containment, recovery, root-cause analysis and notification.
Security controls are tested through vulnerability assessments, penetration tests and independent reviews.
Employees, contractors and the board receive security awareness training appropriate to their roles.
Management measures information security program effectiveness and reports results to the board.
The board and senior management oversee an enterprise-wide business continuity management program.
A business impact analysis identifies critical functions and sets recovery time and recovery point objectives.
Strategies including redundancy, alternate sites and data backup support recovery of critical functions.
Continuity plans are exercised and tested and results are reported and acted upon.
Continuity plans are reviewed, updated and improved after changes, tests and events.
The resilience of critical third-party service providers is assessed and incorporated into continuity planning.
Management maintains an enterprise architecture that aligns technology with business needs.
IT operations are managed through defined procedures for processing, scheduling and operational controls.
Capacity and performance are planned and monitored to meet availability requirements.
Configurations are baselined and controlled and assets are managed through their lifecycle including end of life.
Recurring incidents are analyzed for root cause and resolved.
Development and acquisition projects follow a defined project management and system development life cycle methodology.
Business, security and regulatory requirements are defined before solutions are developed or acquired.
Systems are tested and formally accepted before production implementation.
An independent IT audit function performs risk-based audits under a board-approved audit plan.
Audit and examination findings are tracked to timely remediation and reported to the audit committee.
Service providers are selected after risk-based due diligence.
Contracts define service levels, security, audit rights, confidentiality and termination provisions.
Service provider performance, financial condition and controls are monitored on an ongoing basis.
